boundary_choice.instructions:
A live interpreter is translating this speaker as they talk.
`currentText` is the tail of what they have said that is not translated yet, in their own language.
`stablePrefixChars` is how many leading characters of it the recogniser now treats as settled.
`silenceMs` is the acoustic silence since they last made a sound; null means the microphone level is unknown, which is not the same as zero.
`lastDeltaMs` is how long since the recogniser last added text.
`sttFinal` is true when the recogniser has closed the utterance.
`prosody` is absent when the acoustics are unavailable. When present:
`prosody.terminalPitchSlope` is negative when their pitch falls at the end, which usually means they finished, and positive when it rises.
`prosody.terminalEnergyDrop` in dB is larger when their voice tails off.
`prosody.internalPauseRatio` is larger when they paused a lot inside what they just said.
`prosody.maxInternalPauseMs` is their longest pause inside it.
`prosody.tempoVariability` is larger when their pace is uneven, which often means hesitation.
`prosody.quality` is how trustworthy these acoustic numbers are; treat them as weak evidence when it is low.
`recentTurns` holds a little earlier conversation when it is available.
Pick the one boundary that is safe to translate now, or HOLD. Safe means the text before the boundary is a complete unit of meaning and the speaker is not mid-clause, mid-repair, or trailing into a connective.

HOLD.what: Do not cut anywhere yet. More is coming from this speaker.
HOLD.not_for: Not for a tail that is merely short, and not because `silenceMs` is null. Judge whether the tail itself is finished, not how much text there is.
HOLD.examples: A trailing connective or conjunction; a dangling particle or preposition; a filler such as "uh" or "ええと"; the first half of a self-repair.

C_FULL_28.what: Cut between `before` and `after`. Everything up to the cut is translated and spoken now; the rest waits.
C_FULL_28.not_for: Not when `before` stops mid-clause, and not when `after` carries on the same clause as `before`.

turn_state.instructions: Classify whether the speaker has finished this utterance. Judge the tail of `currentText`, using `silenceMs`, `lastDeltaMs`, `sttFinal` and `prosody` as described in the other questions.

criteria.COMPLETE: Finished. Another person may take the floor.
criteria.CONTINUING: More is coming. The speaker is mid-sentence or mid-clause.
criteria.SELF_REPAIR: Restating. The speaker is correcting what they just said.
criteria.UNKNOWN: Cannot be told from what is available.

safe_to_speak.instructions: Would starting the translated audio right now avoid cutting the speaker off? `tts.active` is true when translated audio is already playing, and `tts.queueDebtMs` is how far behind the queue is. `silenceMs` is null when the microphone level is unknown.

criteria.true: Starting now would not interrupt; the speaker has yielded the floor.
criteria.false: Starting now would talk over the speaker.

repair_likelihood.instructions: Is the speaker about to restate what they just said? Look at the tail of `currentText` for fillers and false starts, and at `prosody.tempoVariability` for an uneven pace.

criteria.true: A self-repair or restatement is likely to follow immediately.
